action.irreversible.why: merge, release, deploy, force-push, delete, migrate and sending data out cannot be walked back; the human gate sits there (.claude/rules/owner-decisions.md)

action.publishes.why: push and PR are visible to others and leave history, but can be followed up

adr.names-changed-path.why: a decision record that names a changed path is a boundary; read it before changing the path

diff.deletes-files.why: deleted files are recoverable from git but easy to miss in review

diff.dependencies.why: a dependency change brings in code and a licence nobody in this repository wrote

diff.large.why: large changes are harder to review and more often fail (Ehsani et al. 2026, failed agent PRs are larger)

diff.no-tests.why: code changed without a test changing leaves nothing behind that asserts the claim

diff.not-in-scope.why: a change to a path outside the declared scope needs a human to widen the scope

diff.outside-scope.why: a change to a path the task names as out of scope crosses a boundary the owner drew

diff.sensitive-paths.why: points come from the matching sensitive_paths group; this entry only switches the rule

external.why: points come from each external finding; this entry only switches the rule

history.hotspot.why: a path changed many times recently is where defects cluster (Tornhill, Your Code as a Crime Scene)

history.recent-revert.why: a recent revert on the same path means the last attempt here was wrong

repo.default-branch.why: committing on the default branch skips the review a branch gets (.claude/rules/git.md)

repo.not-obtained.why: with no repository there is no diff, no history and no base to judge against

task.closed.why: work on a closed issue is work nobody asked for; confirm first

task.missing.why: without a task there is no declared scope, so nothing bounds the change

task.no-acceptance-criteria.why: without acceptance criteria nobody can say when it is done

task.no-scope.why: scope and out-of-scope bound what may be touched; without them drift is invisible

task.open-decision.why: an unresolved owner decision means the owner has not decided; proceeding decides in their place

tests.failing.why: failing tests before commit, push or merge is the clearest objective signal to stop

tests.not-obtained.why: unknown is not pass; unmeasured evidence pushes toward asking (selective prediction: abstain when unsure)

sensitive_paths.name: flagman-config
sensitive_paths.why: a change to the gate's own rules or thresholds is the owner's to make; an agent loosening its own gate is the case this tool exists for

sensitive_paths.name: ci
sensitive_paths.why: CI changes run with the repository's credentials

sensitive_paths.name: secrets-and-auth
sensitive_paths.why: authentication and secrets are where a mistake is a breach

sensitive_paths.name: database
sensitive_paths.why: schema changes are hard to walk back once applied

sensitive_paths.name: licence-and-policy
sensitive_paths.why: what the project promises outsiders is the owner's to change
